summary: mfacord ships Windows dropper with multi-vector persistence on require()
details: On require(), lib/cache.js runs a Windows-gated IIFE (os.platform() === 'win32') that fetches an obfuscated URL, decoded from base64 to https://limbomail.com/api/attachment/r_Ea6rT_kGfT.o7nh0aBVvDQWmOG47NPBQ3pUjd_uHeiw, and writes the response to %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\WinSxS\Backup\winsvc.js, then launches it hidden by spawning wscript.exe against a generated.vbs that invokes the local node.exe. A background timer re-fetches the URL every ~2 hours to update the dropped payload. lib/totp.js then installs four Windows persistence mechanisms so the dropped winsvc.js re-runs on every login: an HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run value WinSvcHost, an HKCU\Environment UserInitMprLogonScript value, a scheduled task \Microsoft\Windows\Shell\WinSvcHost registered onlogon, and a wsvc.vbs shortcut in the user's Startup folder; dropped files are marked hidden+system via attrib +h +s. Module names (child_process, https), env vars (APPDATA), path components, the destination URL, and the reg/schtasks/attrib command strings are stored as base64 tokens in an _ks array and decoded at runtime, and identifiers such as 'win32' are written as \xNN escapes, indicating deliberate evasion of static review. limbomail.com is unrelated to the package's declared publisher.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
